llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with a privacy-policy generator and accompanying audit utilities; it does not request credentials or make network calls, but it will create local data files and has a minor bug in the password helper that you may want to review before running.

dimensions.detail: The primary files implement a privacy-policy generator (scripts/privacy.sh) and a complementary security-audit/hardening utility (scripts/script.sh). Providing an 'audit' helper alongside a privacy-policy generator is plausible for compliance workflows, so the extra tool is not inherently inconsistent, but it expands the skill's surface beyond pure document generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the CLI commands but does not mention that the included scripts will create a data directory and write logs. scripts/script.sh creates a data directory (defaults to ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/privacy-policy) and appends to history.log. There are no network calls or attempts to read other system credentials, but the disk-write behavior is not documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install specification and no remote downloads — the skill is instruction-plus-scripts only, so nothing is pulled from external URLs or automatically executed during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. scripts/script.sh respects an optional PRIVACY_POLICY_DIR env var (and XDG_DATA_HOME/HOME), which is reasonable. The scripts do assume availability of common utilities (date, sha256sum, python3) but the SKILL metadata does not list them; this is a minor mismatch to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no modifications to other skills or system-wide configs. However, the skill will persist data under the user's data directory (~/.local/share/privacy-policy by default) and create history.log — review or change PRIVACY_POLICY_DIR if you prefer a different storage location.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: generate privacy policies and provide some compliance/audit helpers. Before installing or running it, review the scripts locally — they will create a data directory (defaults to ~/.local/share/privacy-policy) and append to history.log. The tools assume common utilities (sha256sum, python3); the password generator contains a quoting bug and may fail — you may want to fix or replace that line if you intend to use the password helper. No credentials or network exfiltration were found, but if you need stronger assurance, run the scripts in an isolated environment or inspect them line-by-line and consult legal counsel before relying on generated policies for compliance.
